records.query: Need scrotal ultrasound findings (mass morphology, vascularity, solid/cystic nature) and serum tumor markers (AFP, hCG, LDH) to confirm malignant scrotal tumor and rule out benign hematocele; histopathology from biopsy remains the definitive diagnostic evidence.
records.text:
Ultrasonography: Revealed a multilocular cyst with septa attached to the testis without testicular abnormalities.
MRI Findings:  Image Title: Pre-operative magnetic resonance Images (MRI)  Image Description: Showed fluid-filled sac (7 cm) and multinodal cyst without solid lesion. No contrast enhanced rim on the cyst. Contents showed high-intensity on T1-weighted image and relatively low-intensity on T1-weighted image consistent with hematoma.
Pathological Examination:  - Gross examination showed two cysts (7.0 cm and 3.0 cm) attached to right testis  - Microscopic examination of smaller cyst showed single row of bland tall columnar cells  - Immunohistochemistry results: EpCAM(+), BerEP4(+), calretinin(−), D2-40(−), WT-1(+), estrogen receptor (ER)(+)(nearly 100%), progesterone receptor (PR)(+)(approximately 20%)  - No intracellular mucin, papillary growth or stromal invasion found.

records.query: Need the patient's scrotal ultrasound report with Doppler assessment (core imaging to characterize the mass, evaluate vascularity, and distinguish solid tumor from hematocele), as well as any prior imaging if available to assess rapid growth. This is essential to confirm or refute scrotal malignancy, given the hemorrhagic aspirate and lack of trauma.

bindings.label: Right scrotal swelling rapidly growing over 3 months without local pain
Patient is a 50-year-old Japanese man, non-smoker, with medical history of hypertension treated with ARB tablet daily and no known allergies
Swelling developed over 3 months with no history of trauma or infections including STDs
Puncture at a prior hospital yielded red-colored fluid; physical examination confirmed right scrotal swelling
Histopathology shows bland tall columnar mesothelial cells with WT-1+/ER+/PR+, calretinin−/D2-40−, no invasion or papillary growth
Ultrasound and MRI reveal a multilocular cystic lesion with septa attached to the testis, lacking solid components or contrast enhancement
MRI signal of the scrotal lesion is consistent with hematoma/hemorrhagic fluid
Scrotal benign multicystic mesothelial lesion (multilocular peritoneal inclusion cyst/cystadenoma)
